issues.description: Field and constructor parameter type mismatch for StockIngredient.price: The problem statement UML (and the solution implementation) declare the price as an int (constructor signature StockIngredient(String, int, int) and getPrice() returning int), but the template repository declares the price as a double (private final double price; constructor StockIngredient(String, double, int); getPrice() returns double). This mismatch affects the same element (StockIngredient.price) across artifacts and will confuse students about which numeric type to use when implementing SealSaloon.calculateTotalPrice and acceptSupplyDelivery, and may lead to unnecessary casts or inconsistent APIs between provided and expected code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the numeric type for StockIngredient.price consistent across all artifacts. The simplest fix is to change the template repository's StockIngredient to use int for price (replace private final double price; constructor parameter type double -> int; and getPrice() -> int) so it matches the UML in the problem statement and the solution. Alternatively, if fractional prices are intended, update the problem statement UML and the solution to use double consistently and adjust calculateTotalPrice and related code to use double sums.
